summary:
Closed (k = +1) universe, momentum-space assignment. REPORT.md was not written (the harness refuses report files from this subagent); this return carries its content. Six scripts with .out files in the folder; all checks pass.
- New constraint: with rho_tau >= 0 (V0[1+cos] >= 0), a turnaround needs a_max >= Omega_m/|Omega_k| (31.5 to 3.15e4 for |Omega_k| = 1e-2 to 1e-5). This excludes 6 of the 20 placeholder grid points. A maximum also needs 2V <= rho_m + 2 rho_r + 4K at H = 0.
- How small momentum space gets: in every sense tied to quanta it is smallest at the turnaround: a~ = 1/a_max; grain hbar c/R0 = 1.44e-34 to 4.5e-36 eV today, divided by a_max; CMB T0/a_max; the CKN cutoff falls as a^-1/2. Closure sets no largest momentum.
- The budget: G M_tot/c^2 = (3 pi/4) R exactly at H = 0, so rho_(l_P) maps the momentum budget onto the radius. This is the Friedmann equation restated.
- Spectra: S^3 harmonics (nu^2 - 1 - s)/R^2, verified from the embedding. On the dodecahedral space the lowest scalar mode is nu = 13 (matches Aurich et al.); the lowest photon (nu = 2) and graviton (nu = 3) modes survive with one helicity only.
- Reciprocity: the Fourier-transform version fails globally on S^3 or T^3; I = omega^-1 H survives on tangent spaces; the local error is (2/3)(sigma/R)^2. The rho_lambda image of our momenta is discrete and unbounded (spacing lambda^2/R), so no closed dual frame arises. As a knob, dual closure is negative dark radiation, |Omega_k~| < 4.9e-6.
- Finite phase space: the DFT equals rho_lambda iff lambda^2 = dx L/2 pi. With dx = l_P and L = 2 pi R, lambda = sqrt(l_P R) >= 149 um, excluded by both of the diameter note's tests. A doubly compact phase space must be torus-like. Grosse-Wulkenhaar Omega <= 1.4e-124.
- Symmetry breaking in finite volume: tunnelling exponent >= 2e125; rotor spacing <= 1.3e-158 eV; nothing observable.

claims.statement: At H = 0 in a closed universe G M_tot/c^2 = (3 pi/4) R exactly, for any content. Since rho_(l_P) maps a momentum M c to the length G M/c^2, at the turnaround the momentum budget in Planck momenta equals (3 pi/4) R_max/l_P. This is the Friedmann equation restated.

claims.statement: The momentum grain of a closed universe today is hbar c/R0 = hbar H0 sqrt|Omega_k|: 1.44e-34 eV at |Omega_k| = 1e-2 and 4.5e-36 eV at 1e-5. It falls as 1/a and is smallest at the turnaround.

On a 3-sphere of radius R: scalars have -lap = (nu^2-1)/R^2 with degeneracy nu^2; transverse vectors (nu^2-2)/R^2, nu >= 2, degeneracy 2(nu^2-1); TT tensors (nu^2-3)/R^2, nu >= 3, degeneracy 2(nu^2-4). Verified from the embedded geometry on invariant subspaces (eigenvalues 2, 7, 6, 13) and matching Hu et al. 1998's q^2 = k^2 + (|m|+1)K.

So the global Fourier version of rho (#11 section 3) fails in a closed universe.

(pure point); cos(2 pi x/L) has spectrum [-1, 1] (continuous): no unitary maps one onto the other'

record_errors: #11 section 3 (and the wiki pages wiki/_index.md, wiki/phase-space/reciprocity/born-reciprocity.md and wiki/phase-space/reciprocity/fourier-transform.md) say 'Quantum kinematics is exactly invariant under rho ... the Fourier transform implements it unitarily'. That holds only when position space is a self-dual group such as R^d. On a 3-sphere or 3-torus it is false globally and holds only locally, to relative order (sigma/R)^2. It is harmless under #11 section 10's flatness assumption and must be restricted if closure is adopted.

Diameter note section 6 and round-5 ruling R11 say 'a closed universe can turn around without negative energy'. That is true but omits two conditions: a_max >= Omega_m/|Omega_k| (because tau's energy is non-negative), and 2V <= rho_m + 2 rho_r + 4K at H = 0.

#1 sections 6 and 10 and #11 section 13 row 10 treat dual curvature k~ as an optional knob. In the slaved-block reading the cotangent fibres are flat, and the conjugate position space is the rho_lambda image of a discrete, unbounded spectrum. Closure of our space therefore produces no closed dual frame, and k~ != 0 needs an unstated compact-momentum postulate. The entry's sign and a^-4 scaling are confirmed.

Diameter note section 4 quotes Grosse-Wulkenhaar's identification of sqrt(Omega) with l_P/(size of the universe) correctly. The source derives it from the minimal momentum sqrt(4 Omega/theta) = 2 sqrt(Omega)/sqrt(theta), so it carries an unstated factor of order 2, and its p^2 spectrum is equidistant, unlike a 3-sphere's. This is a convention-level caveat, not a misquote.
